series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: same-last tick coalescing as book-absorption activity
mechanism: When loading trade ticks, if Last is unchanged from the prior retained print (and optionally still in the same minute), volumes are summed into one position instead of emitting another price event. Author ties this to book absorption: aggression hits the book but price does not move, so millisecond timestamps can stay flat while volume accumulates.
data_needed: Tick CSV with last, volume, flags, time+ms; filter to trade prints
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: WINZ21 Brazilian mini-index futures real ticks; 1-minute bar construction from ticks
why_new_for_mis: Treats unchanged-Last volume aggregation as an explicit absorption/liquidity event class rather than mere data compression for replay speed.
quote: there are several moments when the system just doesn't move, the price stays still, or it could have happened that the Book absorbs every aggression, and the price just doesn't move.

instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: B3 futures tick files; M1 custom-symbol bars
why_new_for_mis: Separates quote-refresh events from trade prints at ingest—usable as a quote-vs-trade activity split for liquidity sensing.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: tick_volume as trade-print count vs real_volume contracts
mechanism: While building M1 bars from ticks, tick_volume increments by 1 per executed trade print (last>0 or volume_real>0), while real_volume sums contract size. Bid/Ask-only quotes do not add to tick_volume. Dual volume measures intensity of trades versus size traded.
data_needed: Ticks with last and volume_real; M1 aggregation
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Exchange-style assets with last+volume; 1-minute bars; author cites ~150 sim ticks vs ~12890 real average tick_volume
why_new_for_mis: Makes explicit the liquidity dual: print-count intensity versus contract volume—MIS can sense busy-thin vs size-heavy minutes independently.
quote: Tick volume is the number of trades that actually occurred within a given bar.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: random first-extreme pivot inside M1 bar sim
mechanism: SimuleBarToTicks flips a coin (rand()&1) to decide whether the bar path seeks low then high or high then low after open, then walks open→first extreme→other extreme→close, optionally subdividing range into NPASS intermediate segments. Removes deterministic open→low bias that EAs could exploit.
data_needed: M1 OHLC + volumes; tick size; rand seed
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 1-minute bars converted to synthetic ticks for replay/sim
why_new_for_mis: Encodes which extreme is visited first as a stochastic intra-bar path attribute; live sensing can measure empirical first-extreme rates as a microstructure regime feature.
quote: now we won't know if the bar will start looking for a minimum or a maximum.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: inter-tick millisecond gap batching as activity clock
mechanism: LoopEventOnTime sums consecutive tick time_msc deltas into m_MountBar.delay and only Sleeps after accumulated delay exceeds ~400 ms (minus overhead). Sub-millisecond bursts are processed without per-tick sleep, so wall pacing tracks tick inter-arrival intensity.
data_needed: Ordered ticks with time_msc; play/pause control flag
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: High-volatility days of real or simulated ticks; M1 bar construction metrics
why_new_for_mis: Uses accumulated inter-arrival ms as an operational activity/volatility clock—transferable as a live burstiness sensor independent of the replay UI.
quote: we will no longer be delaying every tick. Let's accumulate things a little bit and then take a short break.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: Simulation places tick_volume evenly across 60s, sets open/close endpoints, randomly redistributes surplus real_volume, then steps last by ±tick_size with reflection at high/low; if extremes were never hit, forces low/high into mid/late random slots. Free RW (no bounds) is rejected because it violates bar OHLC.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 1-minute bars for any exchange asset used in sim; Excel path plots
why_new_for_mis: Defines constrained ±1-tick pathing inside OHLC as the plausible intra-bar motion model; MIS can score real paths by bound-respect and extreme-hit timing against this null.
quote: we will have to transform a free system into a limited one. ... keeping the RANDOM WALK within the limits previously set by the 1-minute bars.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: three-phase forced RW with channel squeeze and extreme-explosion
mechanism: RandomWalk runs in three zigzag legs (open→first extreme, cross to other extreme, then to close). Channel high/low gradually squeeze toward the leg target; in mid-leg, once both high and low have been touched (bitmask i0==3), bounds re-expand (“explosion”). Final leg alternates bilateral squeeze into a symmetrical/asymmetrical triangle into close.
data_needed: M1 OHLC, tick_volume, tick size; segment sizes ~min(max/3, 0.2*max)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Simulated 1-minute bars; compared graphically to real-looking Price×Time paths
why_new_for_mis: Gives a concrete intra-bar path grammar (first-extreme leg, cross, close triangle) and an extreme-completion bit—usable as sensors of how real tick paths cover a minute’s range.
quote: if the value is 3, then we have an expansion of the boundaries ... If we did not perform this check, the boundaries would close with the random walk compressed to only 3 possible movement positions.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: last-break Bid/Ask channel with rare wider-spread direct orders
mechanism: For simulated ticks, maintain static BID/ASK. When last > ASK, set ASK=last and BID=last−dSpread; when last < BID, set BID=last and ASK=last+dSpread. dSpread is usually 1 tick, occasionally 2 ticks when rand() falls in a high window (~29080–32767), modeling occasional inside-spread “direct” fills without always moving both quotes.
data_needed: Simulated last stream; PointsPerTick; bTickReal flag
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Exchange Last simulation shown in Market Watch; contrasted with real-tick bid/ask
why_new_for_mis: Defines a live microstructure event: last breaking the bid/ask channel plus rare widened-spread direct-order prints—countable liquidity/pressure sensors.
quote: By adding a certain level of randomness to the system, we have enabled the inclusion of direct orders. That is, of the orders that will be executed without changing the BID or ASK.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: interruptible long inter-tick idle as liquidity-gap handler
mechanism: When next-tick gap is large (low liquidity, auction, halt), timer no longer Sleeps the full gap at once. After creating the current bar/tick, remaining idle is drained in ~200 ms slices while checking chart-open and play/pause, so long voids stay interruptible.

instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex and any sparse/halted symbols; multi-hour idle gaps mentioned
why_new_for_mis: Frames multi-second/hour tick voids as a first-class liquidity-gap/halt regime that must remain observable and escapable—usable as a gap-duration sensor.
quote: If for some reason the tick file tells the timer that the symbol should sleep for, say, 15 minutes, the system will be completely locked during that time.
